screens_reviewed: Single capture: 10-audit-weighting.png — Audit wizard step 2 (Youth weighting), top scroll position, captured in the dark theme run.
verdict: The weighting step is well-structured and readable: clear step header, a tappable 9-step navigator, a Youth weighting card with importance options, and a fixed Back/Save/Next footer. But this is the DARK-theme capture and the screen renders the cream LIGHT palette, because the route imports the static `designSystem` constant (locked to lightColors) instead of `useDesignSystem()`. That single bug means the entire screen ignores the auditor's dark preference and is the dominant problem here.

critical_issues.location: app/audit/[placeId]/[step].tsx — module import and every styled node
critical_issues.issue: The audit wizard imports the static `designSystem` constant rather than the live `useDesignSystem()` hook, so all colors resolve to the light/cream palette regardless of the auditor's resolved theme. This dark-theme capture renders cream backgrounds, dark text on light surfaces, and light selection chips — the dark palette (darkColors) is never applied. Theme switching is effectively broken for the entire audit flow.
critical_issues.evidence: pack [step].tsx:23 `import { designSystem } from "lib/design-system";`; core.md lib/design-system.ts:453-460 `export const designSystem = { colors: lightColors, ... }`; getDesignSystem()/useDesignSystem (lib/design-system.ts:477-510) are the theme-aware path and are not used here. Image shows cream surfaces in the dark run.
critical_issues.fix: Replace the static import with `const designSystem = useDesignSystem();` inside AuditStepScreen and thread it (or its colors) into the child components/`getSurveyPalette`/`getStepTone` instead of reading the module-level constant. Those palette helpers and module-scope style functions must become hook-driven (e.g. take `colors` as an argument) so dark/light both resolve at runtime.

improvements.suggestion: The 9-button step navigator sits high in the scroll view (above the fold) and the 'Step 2 of 9' label is also printed twice (pill at :601-607 and progress card at :646-652). On a phone the per-step pills are far from thumb reach and the duplication adds vertical noise. Consider collapsing the redundant 'Step 2 of 9' indicators and/or making the step navigator a compact horizontal-scroll strip so the primary content reaches the fold sooner.
improvements.evidence: pack [step].tsx:592-607 and :646-652 (two 'Step {step} of 9' renders); :669-703 nine wrapped Buttons with minWidth 108. Image shows both indicators plus the full pill grid before the card.

improvements.suggestion: Headline and body sizes are fixed numeric values (e.g. title fontSize={30} at :614, card title fontSize={22} at :1094, question fontSize={16} at :1169) and do not multiply by `designSystem.fontScale`. The header components (YeeStackHeaderTitle) already honor fontScale; the in-body survey text does not, so the auditor's accessibility text-size preference is ignored within the step content.
improvements.evidence: pack [step].tsx:614, :1094, :1169 use raw fontSize; contrast with YeeStackHeaderTitle.tsx:1916-1917 which multiplies by designSystem.fontScale.

tamagui_notes: Heavy use of `style={{ ... }}` escape hatches for color/background/border (e.g. SelectionButton :1300-1304, Card :1084-1088) instead of Tamagui theme tokens; this is a deliberate pattern because the screen drives off the static `designSystem` object rather than Tamagui themes, but it means the Tamagui theme system (defaultTheme from Provider.tsx) is bypassed for this whole flow.

design_system_components_used is (none): the screen hand-rolls SelectionButton, Card, QuestionCard, NoticeCard, Badge-like pills, and a progress bar inline rather than using shared ui/* primitives (e.g. ui/Badge in core.md). The 'Step 2 of 9' pill at [step].tsx:593-608 duplicates Badge styling inline.
SelectionButton intentionally avoids tamagui Button to allow multi-line wrapping ([step].tsx:1284-1286) — a reasonable documented deviation, not a defect.
Spacing largely uses Tamagui space tokens ($3, $3.5, $4) which is good, but screen padding flows through getResponsiveContentContainerStyle(layout, ...) ([step].tsx:434-437) so it stays responsive.
platform_notes: Safe-area: top inset is handled by the native stack header (useYeeStackHeaderOptions, headerShown:true) and the footer adds paddingBottom: bottomInset + 12 ([step].tsx:1680) from useSafeAreaInsets, so the home indicator is cleared. No safe-area defect visible.
Thumb reach: the primary CTA (Next) is in the fixed bottom footer within easy thumb reach ([step].tsx:1718-1744); Back/Save/Next are a 3-up flex row — acceptable on this width.

Status bar: app/_layout.tsx:1369 sets StatusBar style from resolvedTheme=='dark' ? 'light' : 'dark', so the OS status-bar icons would be light, but because the screen body renders cream the dark status-bar/cream-body combination underscores the theme bug.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios (estimated only) — the dark-vs-light rendering bug dominates, so the intended dark-palette contrast cannot be judged from this capture.
Scroll behavior past the fold (only the top position is captured) — completeness of the weighting list, the comments field, and the SectionProgressCard cannot be verified visually.
Runtime states (saving spinner, error NoticeCard, confirm-on-incomplete Alert) are not shown.
Whether dark mode looks correct anywhere in the app, since this single screen is locked to the static light constant.
score_rationale: The layout, hierarchy, spacing, and safe-area handling are solid (would otherwise sit at 7-8), but a verified theme bug (static `designSystem` import at [step].tsx:23, locked to lightColors per design-system.ts:453-460) makes the dark-theme capture render the wrong palette across the entire flow — a significant, user-visible correctness defect that affects every audit screen, landing this in the 3-4 band.
